task: Final Task -- characterise and fix the read path, separate the taper/stage-count knobs, produce final deliverables

established_not_rederived.clock_distribution: Fixed in prior sessions. Write path improved 52-60%; t_write_clock_path is 3.1-9.7% of a 1ns period at every point.
established_not_rederived.read_path_status_before_this_task: Binding at every N (was previously masked by the write path at small N). Part D ratio of 7.60x (before this task's Part B fix) was the READ path's own depth scaling, not a regression.
established_not_rederived.not_a_regression: The original 7.44x ratio was clock-dominated and wrong. The pre-this-task 7.60x was read-dominated and correct, coincidentally close in magnitude.
established_not_rederived.enable_fanout_confound: EnableFanout previously set both stage count and taper ratio at once, making the sweep surface non-monotonic. The 'best' EF value found earlier was a measured configuration, not an optimum -- Part C fixes this by splitting the parameter.

part_a_read_path_characterisation.methodology: Standalone DFFRAM, ElectricalTimingTree::performCritPathExtract(getNet("RDAddr0")) -- bit 0 (LSB) has the worst select-bit fanout (A3) and is BufferCharacteristics.cc's own t_read_addr_path measurement (max over all RDAddr bits). Measured BEFORE the Part B fix (this section characterises the defect); A1's node sequences are the pre-fix state.

sequence_summary: Sel0Inv1.A -> A_to_Y_delay(8.826e-13) -> Y_Ron(2.336e-10) -> Y  [dominant single term]
Mux.SelBuf0 -> [8x unbuffered net-alias passthrough through nested Mux_way0.Sel0, zero delay each hop]
Mux_way0.Out -> way0Out -> Mux2_i4.A -> A_to_Y_delay(1.178e-11) -> Y_Ron(5.083e-13) -> Y  [repeats for i8,i16,i32,i64,i128,i256,i512, 9 levels total]

A1_full_node_sequence.note: Full 87-node and 31-node JSON walks (every A_Cap/A_to_Y_delay/Y_Ron/net hop) were captured via a temporary diagnostic and are summarised here; the SelInv1.Y_Ron line is the single dominant term at N=512, confirming A3 directly (one lumped-RC delay proportional to the FULL accumulated fanout of every downstream MUX2 S0 pin, not distributed across the intervening hops, all of which are bare zero-R/C nets).

N512_B128.dominant_segment: select distribution (Sel0Inv0/Sel0Inv1's own driver stage, specifically Sel0Inv1's Y_Ron RC delay against the full downstream fanout)

N4_B128.dominant_segment: data path (2 series MUX2 hops) -- fanout is tiny (2 leaves share bit 0 at N=4), so the untapered driver isn't yet a problem

A2_delay_split_per_segment.conclusion: Which segment dominates is N-dependent: select distribution dominates at large N (67.8% at N=512) where fanout is large; the data path dominates at small N (85.2% at N=4) where fanout is small enough that even an undersized driver's RC delay is negligible. This is exactly the fanout-driven signature the enable-path fix (Phase 4.1-4.2) already established.

A3_select_distribution_fanout.mechanism: Multiplexer.cc's constructModel(), is_top_level branch (pre-fix: lines ~196-238): each select bit gets exactly 2 fixed-size INVs (Sel%dInv0/Sel%dInv1), producing a net 'SelBuf'+i. That net is then portConnect'd into BOTH mux0 and mux1's own 'Sel'+i port (line ~256-258 originally). At every recursion level BELOW the top (is_top_level==false branch, lines ~264-267 originally), the SAME bit is passed straight through via portConnect(mux0,"Sel"+i,"Sel"+i) -- a bare net alias, zero buffering, zero resistance/capacitance of its own. So one min-size INV pair, at the very top, directly drives (electrically, via the timing graph's cap-summing recursion through however many zero-R/C net hops it takes) every leaf MUX2 S0 pin that uses that bit, anywhere in the whole tree.
A3_select_distribution_fanout.answer: YES -- the select distribution has the IDENTICAL untapered-fanout defect the enable/row-clock chains had before Phase 4.1-4.2: one small, never-resized driver feeding many parallel destinations with zero intermediate buffering.

fanout_by_bit_N512.description: countSelectBitFanout(512, bit) -- number of leaf MUX2 S0 pins driven by each LOCAL select bit (0=LSB). Derived analytically from Multiplexer.cc's own recursive inputs_0/inputs_1/selects_0/selects_1 splitting (bit `selects-1` at any level is consumed by that level's own muxf; lower bits pass to both halves).
fanout_by_bit_N512.worst_case: bit 0 (LSB): 256 leaf MUX2 S0 pins, all driven by one INV pair with zero intermediate buffering -- exactly this bit is what BufferCharacteristics.cc's t_read_addr_path measures as its worst case (RDAddr0).

A4_mux_tree_data_path_sizing.finding: UNIFORM (minimum) size at every level -- muxf (the MUX2 at every recursion level) is created via createStdCell("MUX2",...); construct() with NO subsequent increaseDrivingStrength/setDrivingStrengthIdx call anywhere in Multiplexer.cc, at any recursion depth.
A4_mux_tree_data_path_sizing.reasoning: Every data-path MUX2's own Y output drives exactly ONE downstream node (the next level's single muxf A or B pin -- fanout=1 throughout, confirmed by the downstream_count=1 field on every non-select node in the A1 walk). The bit-duplication case (multiple output-bit copies) is handled by ElectricalDriverMultiplier, which takes the MAX of downstream caps rather than summing, deliberately modelling independent per-bit physical drivers, not a real fanout burden. Since there is no genuine N-way fanout anywhere in the data path, uniform minimum sizing is structurally APPROPRIATE, not a defect -- there is no analogous 'stage k drives fanout k-1's worth of load' tapering opportunity when every stage's real load is a single, small, fixed next-stage input pin.

part_b_fix.decision: APPLIED -- A3 confirmed the same defect exists in the select distribution.
part_b_fix.change_summary: Replaced the fixed 2-INV-per-select-bit chain with a tapered BUF chain per bit (SelBuf<bit>_<stage>), stage count and per-stage sizing computed the same way as DFFRAM's EnBuf/RowBuf chains (largest available drive strength whose own input cap fits a budget shrinking by 1/SelectBufferTaper per stage, working backward from that bit's real fanout load). Fanout per bit computed analytically via countSelectBitFanout(), a pure structural recursion mirroring Multiplexer's own construction. New parameters: SelectBufferStages (0=auto, default) and SelectBufferTaper (default 4). Sizing happens in a new Multiplexer::updateModel() override (previously relied entirely on the base class default sub-instance walk), same reasoning as DFFRAM: must re-run when parameters change, needs the StdCellLib cache. The final stage's output net is still named "SelBuf"+i, so nothing downstream (the mux0/mux1/muxf wiring, and the recursive pass-through at every level below the top) needed to change.

N4_B128.note: Small REGRESSION at the smallest case -- fanout_count(bit=0,N=4)=2, taper=4 -> n_stages=1 (vs the old fixed 2 INV stages). A single BUF stage's own intrinsic delay for this tiny load is not quite as fast as the old fixed 2-INV chain was for this specific tiny-fanout case. Reported, not hidden -- consistent with the same kind of small-N edge-case tradeoff seen in the enable-path taper fix (EnableFanout=0 was sometimes best at the smallest N there too).

part_c_separated_knobs.change: DFFRAM.cc/.h: EnableFanout -> EnableStages (0=auto) + EnableTaper (default 4, also the auto-stage-count log-base). RowClockFanout -> RowClockStages (0=auto) + RowClockTaper (default 4). Taper<=0 disables the corresponding chain (direct connection) -- the old single-parameter's '0 disables' behaviour, moved to the taper knob since the stage-count knob's 0 now means auto. Implemented via a shared computeChainStages() helper, used identically in constructModel()/updateModel()/propagateTransitionInfo().
part_c_separated_knobs.note_on_defaults: Defaults (EnableStages=0, EnableTaper=4, RowClockStages=0, RowClockTaper=4) reproduce the exact same auto-formula the single combined parameter used before -- this is purely a bookkeeping split, not a re-tune. Part D's 'final settings' use these defaults, not the swept best-combination below.

independent_sweep.method: Coordinate search, not a full cross-product: swept EnableStages x EnableTaper at RowClock held at defaults, found the best pair, then swept RowClockStages x RowClockTaper with Enable held at that best pair.
independent_sweep.not_described_as_optimum: This is a MEASURED configuration from a coordinate search over a finite grid ({0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9} stages x {2,3,4,6,8} taper), not a proven optimum -- consistent with the established fact that the discreteness of available drive strengths makes this sweep surface non-monotonic in general.
independent_sweep.not_adopted_as_default: Per instruction ('do not re-tune anything else'), this finding is reported only -- DFFRAM's shipped defaults remain EnableStages=0/EnableTaper=4/RowClockStages=0/RowClockTaper=4.

part_d_final_numbers.d1_full_sweep: 32 points (depth 4-512 x width 32-256), final (default) settings -- see sweep_output/buffer_metrics.json for the complete data (meta includes git hash, tech, frequency, all rate parameters, timestamp, and the 9-item assumptions list including this task's findings).

d2_iso_capacity.distributions: 128x4, 16x32, 1x512 -- all B=128, 65536 total bits, frequency=1e9, timing_opt=false, final (default) settings.
d2_iso_capacity.methodology: area/leakage = per-buffer value x buffer_count (every buffer instance exists in silicon simultaneously). e_read/e_write/t_critical/t_write_clock_path/t_read_path = PER-BUFFER value (a single access touches exactly one buffer).

d3_does_distribution_matter.area: Matters a LITTLE: 5.25% spread. Mechanism: per-instance control-logic overhead (decoder+mux+clock-gating, roughly log2(N)-ish per buffer) plus the new select-buffer chains' own area (more/bigger stages needed at higher per-buffer N) -- both scale with buffer COUNT and per-buffer N respectively, in partially offsetting ways, leaving a small net spread.
d3_does_distribution_matter.leakage: Matters a LITTLE: 5.48% spread, same mechanism as area (leakage tracks silicon footprint).
d3_does_distribution_matter.e_read: Matters A LOT: 154.7x spread. Dominant mechanism: Mux tree depth (ceil(log2(N)) series MUX2 switching stages) PLUS select-buffer chain size (more/bigger stages for higher per-buffer N's fanout) -- both grow with per-buffer N, driving per-access read energy up sharply for the single-large-buffer end.
d3_does_distribution_matter.e_write: Matters A LOT: 92.2x spread. Dominant mechanism: DFFRAM's Write event architecturally sums the clock-gating switching (NAND2/INV) of ALL N rows on every write, not just the addressed one (documented DSENT-ASSUMPTION, DFFRAM.cc: 'why DFF RAM doesn't scale with depth') -- this term scales directly with per-buffer N.
d3_does_distribution_matter.t_critical: Matters SUBSTANTIALLY: 3.24x spread, now entirely due to the READ path (t_read_path_ratio=3.24x, identical to t_critical_ratio, confirming the read path is binding at every point in this comparison) -- NOT the write/clock-enable path (t_write_path_ratio is only 2.24x, and the write path is never actually the binding term at any of the three points). Mechanism: an N:1 mux tree's structural depth (ceil(log2(N)) series MUX2 delay stages plus, before this task's fix, an increasingly-undersized select driver) is a genuine property of a shared-RAM/narrow-mux-tree read architecture. Part of the old gap was an artifact (unbuffered select fanout, now fixed); what remains is real structural depth scaling, not further reducible without a different read-path architecture (e.g. a segmented/indexed read), which is out of this task's scope.
